insight.title: The Late Student Who Solved an Unsolvable Proof
insight.subtitle: How a simple misunderstanding bypassed the limits of human expectation.
insight.notificationHook: How a late student solved the impossible

sections.text: In 1939, graduate student George Dantzig arrived late to his statistics class. He hurriedly copied two equations from the blackboard, assuming they were just his homework assignment.
Finding them slightly harder than usual, Dantzig spent a few days working them out. He finally solved both proofs and neatly dropped them off on his professor’s desk.
Days later, his stunned professor banged on his door. The equations weren't homework; they were two famously "unsolvable" mathematical proofs that world-class scientists had never cracked.
He solved them because nobody told him they were impossible.
